info.name: FinTrack API
info.description:
Generated from backend/docs/openapi.yaml (version 1.1.0) by `npm run docs:postman`. Do not edit by hand.

Runs top to bottom as a scenario with a throwaway account and fictional data. Pick the "FinTrack local" environment
and fill in adminPassword (the demo administrator's password is in backend/scripts/seed-demo.js, development only).
Authentication: requests send the access token from the collection variable accessToken; /auth routes also need
the X-Requested-With header, and the refresh token travels in the ft_refresh cookie, which Postman keeps.

exec: // Dates and a unique throwaway account for each run.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness and readiness probes. No authentication.

request.description:
Liveness probe

Confirms the process is running. Does not touch the database.

Readiness probe

Confirms the database is reachable and reports the applied schema version.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Registration, sign-in, token refresh, sign-out and password reset.

item.name: Create an account and sign in

request.description:
Create an account and sign in

Limited to 10 requests per hour per client. New accounts always get the USER role.

Sign in

Limited to 10 requests per 15 minutes per client. Five wrong passwords in a row lock the
account for 15 minutes. An unknown email and a wrong password return the same 401.
When the account has two-step sign-in on, a correct password returns
`{ mfaRequired: true, challengeToken, expiresInMinutes: 5 }` instead of a session, and no
cookie; complete it with POST /auth/mfa/verify.

item.name: Complete a two-step sign-in with an authenticator or recovery code

request.description:
Complete a two-step sign-in with an authenticator or recovery code

The challenge from /auth/login is valid for 5 minutes, works once and allows 5 attempts.
Wrong codes count towards the same account lockout as wrong passwords. An authenticator
code is accepted once (its 30-second step is remembered); a recovery code ("xxxx-xxxx")
works once, and the user is notified when one is used.

item.name: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token

request.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token

Reads the `ft_refresh` cookie, returns a new access token and replaces the cookie
(rotation). A refresh token works once: presenting an already-used token revokes the
whole session.

Request a password reset link

Always answers 200 with the same message, whether or not the address has an account.
The link is valid for 30 minutes and works once. Limited to 5 requests per hour per client.

item.name: Choose a new password with a reset token

request.description:
Choose a new password with a reset token

Ends every session of the account.

item.name: Transactions
item.description:
Income and expenses. `amount` and `currency` are stored exactly as entered and never
rewritten; `baseAmount` is the value in the user's main currency, with the `exchangeRate`
that produced it. Deleting is a soft delete.

item.name: List, filter, search and page through your transactions

request.description: List, filter, search and page through your transactions

Record an income or expense

Foreign-currency entries are converted with the stored rate snapshot for their date; if
none from the previous 7 days exists, today's rate is fetched and stored first. May raise
budget-threshold and unusual-spending notifications.

item.name: Import rows from a CSV file (preview first, then save)

request.description:
Import rows from a CSV file (preview first, then save)

The web app reads the file and maps its columns; this endpoint takes up to 500 rows per
request. Each row is checked on its own: date (YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future), type,
amount, currency, description, category name (or a fallback category per type), and
payment method (names such as "Card" or "Bank transfer" are accepted). A row matching an
existing transaction (same date, amount, currency and description) is a duplicate.
With dryRun true (the default) nothing is saved and each row comes back as ready,
duplicate or error. With dryRun false, ready rows are saved (duplicates only when
skipDuplicates is false) through the normal path, without a confirmation each; one
summary notification follows. 60 requests per 15 minutes per user.

item.name: Create a weekly, monthly or yearly recurring transaction

request.description:
Create a weekly, monthly or yearly recurring transaction

Occurrence n falls on startDate plus n weeks, months or years (a monthly rule from the
31st uses the last day of shorter months). Occurrences up to today are created at once
(the start may be up to a year back), later ones when the user next opens transactions,
the dashboard or this list. Each is a normal transaction, converted at that day's rate
and created exactly once. Returns { rule, generated }.

item.name: Change, pause or resume a recurring transaction (applies to future occurrences)

request.description:
Change, pause or resume a recurring transaction (applies to future occurrences)

The schedule (frequency and start) is fixed; delete and recreate to change it. Resuming creates missed occurrences.

item.name: Income, expenses, net and savings rate for a period, with the change on the previous period

request.description:
Income, expenses, net and savings rate for a period, with the change on the previous period

Use `month`, or `from` and `to` for any range (the Analytics page sends a day, a
Monday-to-Sunday week, a month or a calendar year). The comparison period:
a day -> the day before; a week -> the week before; a calendar month -> the month before;
a calendar year -> the year before; any other range -> the range of the same length just
before it. While a week, month or year is still running, the comparison stops at the same
point of the previous one.

item.name: Assistant
item.description: AI insights and questions over the signed-in user's own records.

request.description:
Findings about your own spending

Insight cards, unusual expenses (robust z-score and Isolation Forest, each with a reason),
a month-end spending estimate with a range, budget suggestions, regular payments and goal
outlook. Computed by the internal AI service from your records of the last 13 months only.
Limited to 30 calls per 5 minutes per user. Estimates are not guarantees and nothing here is
financial advice.

item.name: Ask a question about your own records

request.description:
Ask a question about your own records

Answered by a rule-based engine from your records only: the response gives `answer`,
`facts` (label and value pairs), the `period` it used, `followUps` and, where relevant, a
`disclaimer`. Investment, tax, loan and insurance questions are declined. Questions are
not stored. Shares the per-user limit with /assistant/insights.
